proposal: The Mandate calls Section 702 an essential tool and recommends that Congress review the PCLOB report to decide whether reforms or codification of administrative changes are needed. For traditional FISA it suggests stiffer penalties for leaks aimed at domestic political targets, tighter controls on intercepts that touch domestic political figures, an express bar on politically motivated use, and better DOJ and FISC accountability.

status_summary: Section 702 was reauthorized with a 2026 sunset by Public Law 118-49 (signed 2024-04-20, before the tracking period), which also added query-approval, audit and penalty provisions that overlap with some Mandate safeguards. In 2026 Congress passed two short extensions, Public Law 119-84 (H.R. 8322, approved 2026-04-18, to 2026-04-30) and Public Law 119-87 (S. 4465, approved 2026-04-30, to 2026-06-12); on 2026-06-11 the House rejected H.R. 9238, which would have extended Title VII to 2026-07-02, by 198 to 218 under suspension of the rules (Roll Call No. 221), and Title VII, including Section 702, lapsed on 2026-06-12, the first lapse since 2008 (CBS News). Collection was reported to continue under FISC certifications approved in March 2026 that run to about March 2027, and the Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as DNI on 2026-07-28 (Roll Call). As of 2026-07-29 reports said the House was out until 2026-08-31 with no Senate plan to act (Punchbowl News), and none of the public laws through 119-118 (2026-09-30) checked on govinfo concerns FISA, so no reauthorization and no new Mandate-style traditional-FISA safeguard was found enacted since the lapse.

timeline.event: FISC recertifies the Section 702 program in March 2026 (exact day not confirmed; month-level date); the certifications are reported to run through about March 2027.

After a House five-year renewal with some reforms failed on 2026-04-16 (200 to 220) and a procedural vote on an 18-month clean renewal also failed, Congress passes a short extension to 2026-04-30; the Senate approves it by voice vote.
Public Law 119-84 (H.R. 8322) is approved, setting the repeal date for FISA Title VII, including Section 702, at 2026-04-30; its amendments take effect on enactment.

Public Law 119-87 (S. 4465) is approved, changing the repeal dates in section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 from 2026-04-30 to 2026-06-12, so Title VII (including Section 702) is extended to that date.
The House fails to pass H.R. 9238, a bill to extend FISA Title VII authorities to 2026-07-02, under suspension of the rules by 198 to 218 (Roll Call No. 221); no further action is recorded.

Section 702 and the rest of FISA Title VII lapse at midnight (12 a.m. on 2026-06-13 per CBS), the first lapse since the authority was enacted in 2008; existing certifications are expected to keep collection going.

Punchbowl News reports that the House has left until 2026-08-31, the Senate has no plan to take up reauthorization before its recess, major telecom providers are still sharing data, and large groups of conservative Republicans and progressive Democrats oppose an extension without new warrant protections. The Senate had confirmed Jay Clayton as DNI on 2026-07-28 by a party-line 51 to 47.
ODNI lists the swearing-in of Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence, the most recent item on its press-release page; no ODNI release on Section 702 reauthorization appears on that page.

The latest public law found on govinfo, Public Law 119-118, does not concern FISA; public laws 119-99 (2026-06-12) through 119-118 that were checked contain no Title VII extension, so the lapse was still unresolved by statute at that date.
